title: Log and trace stores
description: Are VictoriaLogs (CT 121) and VictoriaTraces (CT 122) taking data in and keeping it for 30 days? Open it when a Logs or Traces alert fires, when a board's logs or traces panel is empty, and weekly to see how much of each disk cap is used.

panels.title: Are the stores taking data in?
Logs: up
panels.description: VictoriaLogs answers its health URL and its /metrics scrape works. DOWN means no log is stored and Explore shows nothing (rule HttpProbeFailed: warning after 5 minutes for a standard-tier host; rule TargetDown for the scrape). The senders keep a cursor and catch up after an outage.

panels.title: Logs: ingest rows/s
panels.description: Log lines stored per second, from every node, guest and the hEX. Red at zero mirrors rule LogsIngestionStopped (a 15-minute rate that stays zero for 15 minutes, warning): this tile uses a shorter window, so it turns red first. Every host ships continuously, so zero means shipping is broken.

panels.title: Logs: stored of cap
panels.description: Log data on disk as a share of the 6 GiB hard cap. Red from 5.5e9 bytes is rule LogsNearDiskCap (info, after 1 hour): the oldest days are dropped before the 30-day retention.

panels.title: Logs: rows dropped, 1 h
panels.description: Rows VictoriaLogs refused in the last hour, without the `too_small_timestamp` reason: lines older than the 30-day retention are dropped at ingest by design (a sender replaying its whole journal), so those are not counted. What is left is real: too many fields, a timestamp in the future, debug. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Traces: up
panels.description: VictoriaTraces answers its health URL and its /metrics scrape works. DOWN means spans are refused and the Traces data source shows nothing (rule HttpProbeFailed: warning after 5 minutes for a standard-tier host; rule TargetDown for the scrape). Nothing sends traces yet, so down costs no data today.

panels.title: Traces: stored of cap
panels.description: Trace data on disk as a share of the 16 GiB hard cap. Red from 14.5 GiB is rule TracesNearDiskCap (info, after 1 hour). It reads about 0 % today: no app sends traces yet, only the 6 rows of the smoke test are stored.

panels.title: Traces: rows dropped, 1 h
panels.description: Spans VictoriaTraces refused in the last hour (too many fields, a timestamp in the future, debug; spans older than retention are expected and not counted). Zero today because nothing sends. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Stores read-only
panels.description: 1 when either store has put itself in read-only mode and rejects writes, which a store does when its disk is nearly full. Should be 0. No alert mirrors it: LogsNearDiskCap and TracesNearDiskCap fire earlier, at the retention cap.

panels.title: Logs: rows ingested, by source
panels.description: Log lines stored per second: `journald` from the nodes and guests (systemd-journal-upload), `syslog_udp` from the hEX. Both should be steady above zero: a source that goes flat is shipping broken (rule LogsIngestionStopped fires only when the total is zero).

panels.title: Logs: rows dropped in the last hour, by reason
panels.description: Rows refused, counted over a trailing hour. `too_small_timestamp` is expected: a sender that replays its journal sends lines older than the 30-day retention. `too_many_fields`, `too_big_timestamp` and `debug` are real: a sender with a broken clock or a runaway field set. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Logs: HTTP requests and errors
panels.description: RED for the store's HTTP API: requests per second by path (only paths with traffic are drawn; the journald upload carries nearly all of it) and the error rate. A rising error line is senders getting rejected. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Logs: journald upload latency
panels.description: How long VictoriaLogs takes to answer a journald upload (a summary exported by the store: the median and the 99th percentile of its recent requests). Milliseconds is normal; seconds means the disk or CPU of CT 121 is saturated. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Logs: stored against the cap
panels.description: Log data on disk against the 6 GiB hard cap. The dashed line is 5.5e9 bytes, rule LogsNearDiskCap (info, after 1 hour): above it the oldest days are dropped before the 30-day retention. Compressed logs are small: far below the cap is the normal state.

panels.title: Logs: oldest log kept
panels.description: Age of the oldest stored log line, in days. It climbs to the 30-day retention (dashed) and stays there. If it stops short of 30 while the stored size is near the cap, the cap is cutting retention short (rule LogsNearDiskCap).

panels.title: Free disk space, logs and traces
panels.description: Free bytes on each store's data disk. The hard caps (6 GiB, 16 GiB) leave room on the 10 GB and 20 GB disks; a free-space line that falls toward zero with the stored size far below its cap means something else is filling the CT. No alert mirrors it (HostFilesystemFull covers nodes and the monitoring CT).

panels.title: VictoriaTraces (CT 122): what comes in and what is kept
Traces: ingest, rows and requests per second
panels.description: Spans stored per second, insert requests per second and request errors. No app sends traces yet, so the rows series does not exist (vt_rows_ingested_total appears with the first span) and the request lines sit at zero: that is expected. Once a sender exists, a flat line while it runs means spans are refused. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Traces: rows dropped in the last hour, by reason
panels.description: Spans refused, over a trailing hour: `too_many_fields`, `too_big_timestamp`, `too_small_timestamp` (older than retention), `debug`. All zero until an app sends. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Traces: stored against the cap
panels.description: Trace data on disk against the 16 GiB hard cap. The dashed line is 14.5 GiB, rule TracesNearDiskCap (info, after 1 hour): above it the oldest days are dropped before the 30-day retention. A few KB today: only the smoke-test span is stored.

panels.title: Stores: CPU, share of one core
panels.description: CPU each store process uses, as a share of one core (both CTs have one core). Near 100 % for long means ingest or queries are CPU-bound and uploads slow down. Idle stores sit near zero. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Stores: resident memory
panels.description: Memory each store process holds. CT 121 has 512 MiB of RAM and CT 122 has 1 GiB (proxmox/opentofu/logs.tf, traces.tf): the process's own memory-limit metric reports the host's RAM seen through the CT, so no limit line is drawn. A line that climbs toward its CT's RAM ends in an out-of-memory kill. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Stores: insert concurrency limit reached
panels.description: Times an insert had to wait because every insert slot was busy (the store's concurrency limit). Occasional ones are fine; a steady stream means senders are queueing behind a saturated store. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Stores: rows pending
panels.description: Rows accepted but not yet searchable: a store buffers them for a few seconds before they are queryable (the smoke test waits for this). A number that keeps rising instead of returning to zero means the store cannot flush as fast as rows arrive. Zero for the trace store while nothing sends. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: The stores' own warnings and errors
Stores: warnings and errors logged, by level
panels.description: Lines the two store processes logged above info level, counted from their own metrics, which works even when log shipping is down. A few warnings at start-up are normal; a steady stream of errors means look at the lines below. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Stores: errors in their own logs
panels.description: Error and critical lines from CT 121 and CT 122 (VictoriaLogs ships its own journal to itself, so this panel is empty when the log store is down: use the metrics panel above then). Empty is good. Not checked by --verify-live.
